name: 1.000+ Project week
description:
TUM Dances! is an initiative of the TUM Center for Culture and Arts and the TUM School of Medicine and Health (Applied Sport Science) that aims to make dance accessible and tangible in all its diversity. Through workshops, performances, and project-based formats, the initiative creates a space for dance as an art form at the intersection of academic inquiry, social participation, and holistic health promotion. The events invite participants not only to experience dance as spectators but also to engage actively through movement. Together, we foster opportunities for encounter, creativity, and reflection. The overarching aim of TUM Dances! is to make dance accessible and experiential for the TUM community as an integral component of cultural and aesthetic education.

One of the project's formats is the Community Dance Project Week for Students. Open to students from all TUM Schools, the project offers participants the opportunity to experience and shape dance as an artistic and cultural practice. Throughout an intensive project week, students work alongside two instructors and dance artists to create a professional artistic dance performance, which is presented to an audience at the end of the week.

The project week, including the final performance, is planned and delivered by Dr. Tina Schwender (Head of Gymnastics and Dance, TUM) in cooperation with Dr. Ellen Steinmüller from ExisTanz gUG. This non-profit social enterprise is dedicated to creating opportunities for non-professionals to engage with high-quality dance art as a catalyst for personal and social transformation. The ExisTanz concept is based on the Community Dance methodology developed by Dance United, an innovative British dance organization. The development and delivery of the projects are guided by the professional working and performance practices of contemporary dance and are founded on three core principles:

- Professionalism in both the working and performance environment
- Intensity of engagement through daily, extended rehearsal periods
- Goal orientation through a performance-based approach

During the creation phase of the project week, participants take part in approximately 4.5 hours of rehearsal each day. Alongside the development of the performance piece, participants gain experience in areas such as contemporary dance technique, teamwork, and non-verbal communication skills.
The project concludes with a structured reflection session, providing participants with the opportunity to reflect on and share their experiences with others. Guiding questions may include: What have you learned (about yourself)? What insights or experiences will you take away from this project?

Exam mode: Presentation (10-15 min); learning portfolio (10.000-20.000 characters)

Introductory Workshop at TUM Campus olympic parc (90 minutes):
Interested participants are introduced to contemporary dance techniques and fundamental choreographic principles. Registration for the introductory workshop can be completed via email at: tina.schwender@tum.de.
Participation in the project is also possible without attending the introductory workshop.
prerequisites: Participation open to everyone (with and without dance experience)!
